profile.entities: Greenpanel Industries Ltd; Greenpanel AP Plant
profile.themes: Middle East War supply shock; Chemical cost inflation; Volume-led market share gain; Margin defense via price hikes

bull_bear.body: Priority: Debt reduction and strengthening balance sheet. No dividends mentioned; cash flow directed towards deleveraging post-FX shock.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical (Middle East war) disrupting exports and spiking chemical/freight costs; Competitive discounting eroding price hike benefits; FX volatility on Euro debt; New competitor capacity (400k cum) coming online in H2FY27.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic on volumes, defensive on margins; Transparent about one-offs (FX, startup costs); Pragmatic on capex pause.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: DSO increased to 21 days (from 11) due to abnormal March end-sales stocking and higher OEM/export mix, though still best-in-class; Thin MDF capacity is fungible across lines, not dedicated, explaining lower specific utilization metrics; 15% price hike effective mostly from Q1FY27, not Q4FY26.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Reported net debt reduced to Rs 141 Crs (down ~15 Crs vs 31-Mar-26 at Rs 156 Crs and Rs 233 Crs at 30-Jun-25).
- Credit ratings for working capital facilities reaffirmed by ICRA at A+.
- Cash conversion cycle stood at 42 days vs 38 days at 31-Mar-26; the deck says working capital rose to factor monsoon seasonality but is still lower than the same period last year.
- Management states leverage and available liquidity remain comfortable to support growth.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: MDF: Domestic vol +29.5% Q4, +16.9% FY26; Total vol (incl. exports) +27.8% Q4, +12.9% FY26. Realizations down 3.6% FY26 due to mix/OEM. High-value mix: 43% vol, 55% value. Plywood: Vol +18% Q4, flat FY26. Exports halted in March due to Middle East war/freight.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chemical cost inflation + supply chain disruption from Middle East war | Unhedged import-dependent panel makers | loser | High | Companies without long-term chemical contracts or export exposure face immediate margin compression. |
| Capacity addition (400k cum) in H2FY27 increasing supply | Small unorganized MDF players | loser | Med | Consolidation likely as large players like Greenpanel use scale to defend share via volume strategy. |
| Shift to multi-species timber reducing Eucalyptus dependency | Greenpanel Industries Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Early mover in raw material rationalization gains cost advantage over peers stuck on single-species sourcing. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Cover slide claims the company is "INDIA'S LARGEST WOOD PANEL MANUFACTURER".
- Business is presented in two reported segments — MDF (net sales Rs 316.8 Cr in Q1FY27) and Plywood (Rs 33.2 Cr) — with MDF the dominant contributor.
- Brand-building is treated as a structural lever: national TV integrations across 6 news channels, sustained trade-publication presence, 120+ PR placements and participation at Bharat Buildcon 2026; recognised as one of the "Most Trusted Brands 2026-27" by Team Marksmen Daily and listed by Silicon Homes Magazine among the Top 10 Wooden Flooring Brands.
- Distribution/brand reach cited: activations across 900+ retail outlets, 2K+ dealer brandings, 200+ in-shop brandings and 100+ carpenter & contractor meets.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Exports] "Zero Export sales" during Q1FY27 due to the ongoing war in the Middle East since March 2026 — the deck repeats this on multiple slides as the reason total MDF volumes fell despite domestic growth.
- [FX exposure] The company carries Euro-denominated borrowings tied to the new MDF plant, producing an exceptional FX line (Rs -25.5 Cr in Q1FY26, Rs -1.0 Cr in Q1FY27) that sits outside Operating EBITDA.
- [Other income] EPCG income was Rs 5.1 Cr in Q1FY26 and Rs 6.2 Cr in Q4FY26 but NIL in Q1FY27, per the deck's own footnote.
- [Digital] New website launched, with 25K+ website visits, 59K+ page views, 5.4M+ digital impressions and 450+ qualified leads cited for the quarter.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Chemical costs (40-45% of RM) up 40-45%; Timber stable. 15% price hike implemented to offset inflation, though discounting by competitors may dilute full realization. Raw material mix rationalization (shifting from Eucalyptus) ongoing to protect margins.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Early double-digit to mid-teens (industry pace); Margin: Maintain or improve over FY26 high-single digits (no specific figure due to chemical volatility); Order Inflow: Focus on volume share gain; Capex: INR20-30cr (sustenance only), no major expansion planned in FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: N/A (Commodity/Stock production model); Management highlighted 60% capacity utilization in Q4, implying significant organic volume headroom without new capex.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Underutilized capacity (40% headroom) allows volume scaling without capex; New high-margin products (Boil Black, HDWR doors) driving value mix; Plywood capacity expansion possible only after current lines fully utilized.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Greenpanel delivered strong volume growth (MDF +29.5% YoY in Q4) driven by channel engagement and new product launches, but reported a net loss (PAT -INR29.1cr FY26) due to INR49cr FX losses on Euro debt and new plant stabilization costs. The near-term narrative shifts to defending margins via a 15% price hike against volatile chemical costs while pausing capex to deleverage.
